title: RAII and scope-based extinction
concept: When a C++ object goes out of scope, its destructor is automatically called to clean up resources.

steps.title: Create Guard object
steps.explanation: `g` is created and its constructor is called. It's time to acquire resources.

steps.title: Perform work
steps.explanation: Use resources safely while the object is alive.

steps.title: Scope termination and automatic cleanup
steps.explanation: `main` ends and `g`'s destructor is automatically called. This is the core of RAII.

quiz.question: What is the most correct core description of the RAII pattern?
options: Automatic cleanup by tying resource management to object lifespan
Destructors are never called in exception situations.
quiz.explanation: RAII reduces leakage by linking resource acquisition/release with object creation/destruction.

misconceptions.wrong: You must call free/delete directly before the return statement.
misconceptions.correct: The destructor of a stack object is automatically called when scope ends.
misconceptions.why: This is because C++ provides object lifecycle-based resource management.

keyTakeaway: RAII increases stability with the rule that 'resources are alive only as long as the object is alive.'
